title: Kyrie Irving Embraces the Mavericks' Rebuild Around Cooper Flagg
htmlContent:
Kyrie Irving isn't pretending the Dallas Mavericks are the same team he joined three and a half years ago. Speaking after the club's first training camp practice on Saturday, the 34-year-old guard openly described the franchise as being in a period of restructuring and rebuilding, with teenage star Cooper Flagg at the center of it.

Rather than bristle at the shift, Irving framed it as an opportunity. He said the organization has a clear direction and that his job is to fit into it, not redefine it.

A Leader Returning From Injury

Irving has not played since tearing the ACL in his left knee in February 2025. As he works his way back, he said his priorities are straightforward: lead, stay unselfish, and prepare well enough to keep playing at an elite level.

He was careful not to set bold public targets, noting that his words tend to get twisted once they leave the practice gym. Still, he hinted that the group believes it can catch people off guard.

"The next stage of my career is still being written," Irving said.

A Franchise Remade Since His Arrival

The Mavericks Irving joined in a February 2023 trade look almost nothing like today's version. At the time, Mark Cuban held controlling ownership, Nico Harrison ran basketball operations, Jason Kidd was on the sideline, and Luka Dončić was the face of the franchise.

Every one of those pieces has since moved. Governor Patrick Dumont dismissed Harrison last November and, after a six-month search, brought in Masai Ujiri as president and alternate governor. One of Ujiri's first significant moves was parting ways with Kidd, and Dallas named Dusty May its new head coach in June.

Irving didn't sugarcoat the upheaval, acknowledging that the stretch has felt chaotic at points.

Building Chemistry With Cooper Flagg

Through all the turnover, Irving has stayed a steady presence. He spent time this summer working out alongside Flagg in Las Vegas, Los Angeles, and Durham, North Carolina, and he organized a team mini-camp in Southern California earlier this month.

He admitted he can't yet say exactly what the finished product will look like, but said he is ready to turn the page and help build something new.

The 15-year age gap between Dallas's two most talented players has drawn plenty of attention, but the front office sees a natural on-court fit. Ujiri has expressed genuine curiosity about how the pairing will play out, and Irving said nobody in the building is treating this season as a throwaway. The team, he said, holds itself to high expectations.

Dallas Held On Despite Trade Interest

Irving's name surfaced in trade conversations over the summer. Brandon Scoop B' Robinson mapped out several trade packages back in June and potential suitors for Irving's services. The Athletic later reported that the Mavericks turned away the offers, signaling that they view Irving as part of their plan rather than a trade chip.

Contract Status and the Road Ahead

Irving is earning $39.5 million this season and has a $42.4 million player option for next year. Asked whether he hopes to finish his career in Dallas, he said much of that is beyond his control and described it as a collaborative decision.

He added that he plans to use his years of experience to inform conversations with Ujiri, general manager Mike Schmitz, and the coaching staff. As for the constant discussion of his age relative to Flagg's, Irving said it doesn't bother him. His focus, he said, is on continuing to develop and giving his best to his teammates.

For a franchise that has overhauled nearly everything in less than a year, Irving represents rare continuity. If he returns healthy and meshes with Flagg the way Dallas expects, the Mavericks' rebuild could move faster than many observers anticipate.
excerpt: Kyrie Irving spoke openly after the Mavericks' first training camp practice about Dallas's rebuilding era centered on teenage star Cooper Flagg, his ACL recovery, his summer workouts with Flagg, and his role as a veteran leader within a franchise that has overhauled nearly every key piece in under a year.
